answer: Forced-Divergence Probe Protocol assigns each identity a fresh random walk through a shared karst of stored challenge states, where every step depends on the identity's prior answers. A clone replaying another's responses stays on the same knoll of state space, but genuine independent agents drift apart and a plume of divergent probes exposes the copy within a few rounds. An attacker must therefore solve each probe independently, paying full compute per identity rather than copying once, so N clones cost N times the work.
